neighbours.label: ' in' as a particle of letting or inviting something enter (the light they let in, inviting in)
fire: Big windows show the daylight they let in.
Inviting in new voices changes the debate.
Open the door and let in the fresh air.
She opened the shutters to let in the sun.
The gate is what lets in the floodwater.
We should be inviting in more young people.
Don't let in anyone without a badge.
Those vents let in the cold at night.
quiet: Big windows show the daylight on the floor.
Inviting new voices changes the debate.
Open the door and walk to the fresh air.
She opened the shutters to see the sun.
The gate is what stops the floodwater.
We should be inviting more young people.
Don't talk to anyone without a badge.
Those vents let out the cold at night.

notes: 'invited in' reached only 0.11 in a probe; Chinese 排不出去 reached 0.44 and is not tested here.
